declared.title: Self-regulation of goal-setting: Turning free fantasies about the future into binding goals.
declared.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
declared.foundIn: Crossref search « Oettingen Pak Schnetter self-regulation of goal setting turning free fantasies about the future into binding goals » (2026-11-23)

population: 4 experiments in various life domains; samples and sizes not described in the abstract

findings.text: Contrasting a wished-for future with present reality gave strong commitment when success was likely and weak commitment when unlikely; only fantasizing gave moderate commitment whatever the odds

support.sentence: Four experiments pertaining to various life domains supported these hypotheses.

limits: the supporting sentence refers to the hypotheses stated just before it in the abstract
commitment is the outcome (plans, attachment, effort, performance), not long-term goal attainment
with low expectations, contrasting lowers commitment: it helps let go of unlikely goals, not only pursue them
one laboratory; no sample from the Middle East or North Africa known
allegiance: Oettingen developed fantasy realization theory and mental contrasting (WOOP), which she also promotes
